constraints: Prompt content includes end-user text, so any hosted option must offer a data-processing agreement with no training on customer data; self-hosting removes the question entirely
Usable regression results are needed within three weeks
Whatever is chosen must support custom scoring logic, not only built-in metrics
Budget ceiling for tooling this year is modest — roughly one engineer-month of fully loaded cost

options.label: Build an in-house eval harness
options.summary: A small internal tool: dataset store, runner against the team's own model endpoints, custom scorers, and a results diff view.

options.label: Adopt an open-source eval framework and extend it
options.summary: Take a maintained open-source framework, self-host it, and write the team's custom scorers and reports as extensions.

options.label: Buy a hosted eval platform
options.summary: A commercial platform with hosted UI, annotation workflows, and managed scaling, under a DPA.

question: A three-engineer AI team needs LLM output evaluation (regression testing prompt changes, custom scorers, a human review queue). Should it build in-house, adopt and extend an open-source framework, or buy a hosted platform?
stakes: Evaluation is the team's release gate: if the harness is wrong or unused, prompt regressions ship silently. The wrong tooling choice costs either months of engineer time or a recurring bill for a shelf product.
